extracted.intended_audience: media researchers, journalists, news editors, and media-quality auditors
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Westerståhl's decomposition of objectivity into measurable sub-dimensions (factuality and impartiality) to evaluate or design news selection and homepage presentation. Use the model's operational criteria (verifiability, relevance, source/quote balance, tonal neutrality) as auditable metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity (composite)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectivity is not a single norm but a composite construct made up of separate, measurable components (factuality and impartiality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use decomposition to measure each component separately as a quality-audit tool for news selection systems or homepages; an objective system must produce acceptable scores on each axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factuality
rubrics_metrics.description: A dimension of objectivity covering the correspondence between report content and verifiable facts; encompasses truth and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether content is accurate and verifiable (truth) and whether the chosen facts bear on important social issues or decisions (relevance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth
rubrics_metrics.description: The story should be accurate, verifiable, and free of fabrication. Operationalized as correspondence between report content and verifiable facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer documented, checkable events and facts; flag fabrications or unverifiable claims. This is the basis for the 'verifiability premium.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: The story should select information that matters to the public — i.e., that bears on important social issues, decisions, or events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply a 'relevance filter' to demote true but trivial items; relevance is an intrinsic part of objectivity (truth ≠ relevance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: A dimension of objectivity covering fair treatment of competing parties and neutral presentation; includes balance/non-partisanship and neutral presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether reporting allows equal treatment of perspectives and avoids advantaging any side through sourcing, framing, tone, or visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance / Non-Partisanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Equal treatment of competing parties or perspectives; neither side systematically advantaged in airtime, source counts, or favorable framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure source counts, airtime/space, and framing effects; recognize that reporters may select stories partly because they admit balanced treatment, so univocal voices tend to be under-covered or reframed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The framing, tone, language, and visual treatment should not advantage any side. Even balanced quotes can be undermined by tilted framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit headlines, leads, imagery, and story frames for loaded language or visual cues that steer audience interpretation; prefer tonal neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiability Premium
rubrics_metrics.description: An operational selection criterion: items whose facts can be independently checked are more reportable (e.g., documented events > rumored events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give higher newsworthiness to events and claims with independent documentation; use verifiability as a gate for homepage placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance Filter (operational)
rubrics_metrics.description: An operational criterion that demotes true but trivial items; stories must pass the relevance test to be prioritized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement explicit thresholds for social importance or decision-relevance when selecting items for prominence; record rationale for inclusion/exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source Balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories are selected partly because they admit balanced sourcing (e.g., disputes with clear two sides are easier to report objectively than one-voice condemnations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer stories that permit representation of competing perspectives; measure the presence and parity of sources as part of selection/audit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote Symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: In selection and editing, quote counts should match (symmetry of quoted voices across sides).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count and compare quotes attributed to opposing perspectives; ensure editing does not disproportionately truncate or foreground one side's quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tonal Neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories framed in non-loaded language are preferred to stories that require taking a side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess lexical tone, evaluative adjectives, and framing devices; avoid headlines and leads that presuppose judgments or value-laden descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurability / Decomposition advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: The four components (truth, relevance, balance/non-partisanship, neutral presentation) can be measured separately, making the model usable as a quality-audit tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design separate indicators and scoring rules for each component to allow systematic auditing of homepage or newsroom selection decisions and cross-national comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth-versus-Relevance principle
rubrics_metrics.description: An explicit principle: truth is not equivalent to relevance — an item can be true but irrelevant, and relevance is part of objectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When scoring factuality, treat veracity and public importance as distinct axes; avoid elevating trivial true facts to prominence.
